title: Focus Cards 1.2.0: Home Screen Cards and Layout Controls
meta_description: Focus Cards 1.2.0 adds configurable Home Screen cards, spacing and color controls. Check its official source for current compatibility details.
summary: Focus Cards is described by its package metadata as a Home Screen customization tweak built around configurable cards, spacing controls and color options. Version 1.2.0 is listed for both iphoneos-arm64 and iphoneos-arm64e architectures. Those architecture labels identify the available package variants, but they do not by themselves confirm support for every device or jailbreak setup. Readers should compare their environment with the official source information before installing either variant.
what_it_does: Adds configurable cards to the Home Screen according to the package description.
Includes controls related to card spacing.
Includes color options for the card presentation.
Uses PreferenceLoader as one of the listed dependencies, indicating that configuration is expected through a settings interface.
Provides separate package variants for iphoneos-arm64 and iphoneos-arm64e environments.
compatibility_note: The supplied metadata lists iphoneos-arm64 and iphoneos-arm64e variants and includes a tag indicating a minimum of iOS 16.0. This information does not confirm every device, later system release, bootstrap or jailbreak combination. Check the architecture used by your package manager, read the developer's current notes, and do not treat the presence of a package variant as a guarantee that it matches your particular setup.
installation_steps: Open your package manager and confirm that the official Example Developer Repo is already configured and refreshing without errors.
Open the Focus Cards package page and verify that it shows version 1.2.0 from the expected developer and source.
Compare the offered architecture with your jailbreak environment; select only the iphoneos-arm64 or iphoneos-arm64e variant that your setup requires.
Read the package description, dependencies, price information and any compatibility notes shown on the official source before confirming installation.
Allow the package manager to resolve its listed dependencies, including PreferenceLoader, without adding replacement packages from an unrelated source.
After installation, follow only the respring or restart instruction presented by the package manager, then locate the tweak's settings before changing several options at once.
safety_notes: Create a current backup and keep access to your package manager before changing Home Screen components.
Do not install both architecture variants, and do not obtain a repackaged binary from an unofficial download page.
If the developer page does not explicitly cover your exact setup, treat compatibility as unconfirmed rather than assuming support.
Change one setting at a time so that an unwanted layout result can be traced and reversed more easily.

faq.question: What does Focus Cards 1.2.0 change?
faq.answer: Its supplied package description says that it adds configurable cards to the Home Screen and includes spacing and color controls. The metadata does not provide a complete catalogue of every setting, so the official package page remains the place to confirm the current option list.

faq.question: Which package architecture should be installed?
faq.answer: The feed lists iphoneos-arm64 and iphoneos-arm64e variants. Use only the variant required by your jailbreak environment and package manager. If you cannot identify that environment confidently, verify it before installing rather than selecting a package by trial and error.

faq.question: Is support for every iOS 16 device confirmed?
faq.answer: No. A supplied tag indicates a minimum of iOS 16.0, but the metadata does not confirm every device, system point release, bootstrap or jailbreak combination. Consult the developer's current compatibility notes for your exact setup.

faq.question: Where should the package be obtained?
faq.answer: Use the official developer repository shown on the page. Avoid mirrors and repackaged files because their contents and update path cannot be established from the supplied package metadata.
